Quick triage notes (initial pass):
- I pulled the attached chunk traces and sampled the server kernel logs. We see a pattern where the server emits the first data chunk and then the connection's chunked transfer stream doesn't flush further frames for 20–40s. The HTTP layer returns 504 on connection close from the proxy.
- Two plausible contributing factors: 1) proxy buffer backpressure from an upstream proxy (we saw 502/504s clustered on a subset of nodes), 2) KV-cache thrashing for long-context sessions under the demo workload (sequence lengths spike).
- The traces show the chunk frames reach our application thread, but the write syscall blocks intermittently — suggesting a socket-level backpressure / proxy queuing problem, not pure model compute.

Immediate mitigations I can push in the next 30–45m (if we want to be aggressive):
- Route ClearedHealth traffic to the standby region pool (warm fallback) to see if the failure rate drops (fast rollback available).
- Increase socket write timeout and add proactive chunk-heartbeat frames (short 100ms keepalive frames) for their route to avoid silent windows.
- For demo-critical sessions, temporarily fallback to non-streaming (batch) response endpoint while we root cause.

I recommend route failover first (lowest risk) + CS coordination. Full RCA will require deeper proxy and network capture; I'll request infra to correlate proxy logs right now.

— Soojin
